notes: No genuine Bestsellers-type PLP found on jysk.dk after real investigation. ACCESS: direct HTTP fetch, no WAF (confirms prior pass). CHECKED: (1) Homepage HTML including its full embedded i18n translation dictionary, which contains essentially every UI string used site-wide -- searched for popul*, bedst*, mest solgte, mest popul*, bestseller, trending, kundefavorit, toppen af poppen, favorit. Hits were all non-PLP UI strings: 'MEST POPULAERE SPOERGSMAAL' (Most Popular Questions -- an FAQ label), 'Sorter efter bedste anmeldelser' (sort-by-best-reviews, a per-category sort option not a listing page), and 'Favoritter' (a user wishlist/favourites feature, not a bestseller merchandising page). (2) Full site sitemap.xml (~2880 URLs) grepped for best/popul/salg/nyhed/outlet/favorit/top-sal/mest -- no bestseller-shaped URL exists; the only 'favorit' hits are editorial /inspiration/ blog posts like 'indkoeberens-moebel-favoritter' (buyer's picks articles, not product listings). (3) Direct URL probes for /bestsellere, /populaere-produkter, /mest-solgte-produkter equivalents all returned 404. (4) Confirmed /nyheder (New Arrivals) and /outlet (Clearance) are the only two merchandising-concept PLPs on the site; no third 'Bestsellers' sibling exists alongside them, in nav or sitemap. Conclusion: JYSK Denmark does not expose a bestseller/most-popular merchandising PLP; only a per-category 'sort by best reviews' option, which is not a listing page per Sec.3 of the brief.
